justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a mildly bullish but essentially flat trajectory from what appears to be a current price near 133–134. For the 1-day estimate, I anchored closely to the prevailing price level, assuming mean-reversion tendencies dominate over very short horizons and that no major scheduled catalysts were imminent. The 1-week estimate nudges slightly higher, reflecting a modest positive drift assumption consistent with longer-run equity market trends and the absence of strong bearish technical signals. The 1-month estimate continues that gentle upward drift, incorporating the historical tendency for broad equity indices or individual securities to trend slightly positive over multi-week periods in the absence of structural headwinds.

The confidence interval widths grow progressively wider as the horizon extends, which is standard given that uncertainty compounds over time. For the 1-day window, I drew on typical daily volatility ranges — a move of roughly plus or minus 2–3 points captures the vast majority of ordinary daily fluctuations. Over a week, realized volatility can accumulate meaningfully, so I widened the band to roughly plus or minus 6 points. At one month, macro developments, earnings surprises, or sentiment shifts can produce swings of 10% or more, so the interval expands to reflect that broader distribution of plausible outcomes.

Specific risks that could push outcomes outside these intervals include sudden macroeconomic data surprises — a hotter-than-expected inflation print or a sharp deterioration in labor market data — which could reprice rate expectations and move markets well beyond my stated bounds. Geopolitical shocks, credit events, or an unexpected earnings miss from a systemically important company could also generate tail moves. On the upside, a decisive dovish pivot from a major central bank or a blowout economic report could drive a sharp rally beyond my upper bounds.

It is also worth acknowledging that my estimates carry model uncertainty on top of market uncertainty. I do not have real-time data, so my starting price anchor may itself be slightly stale, which introduces a baseline error that propagates through all three horizons. If the true current price differs meaningfully from my assumed anchor, all estimates and intervals should be shifted accordingly.
